summary: Recorded TG-6F guarded GitHub Actions and AWS lifecycle validation

assertions: GitHub Actions lifecycle graph is discoverable in normal runs and validates the local-github-action scaffold without requiring cloud infrastructure.
GitHub Actions graph covers first deploy, existing deploy reuse, reset, explicit destroy guard behavior, and skip-destroy/keep-alive behavior using CI-safe markers and context projection.
AWS lifecycle graph is discoverable in normal runs.
Without explicit selection and credentials, AWS graph records a guarded skip/fail-fast result and creates no cloud resources.
With explicit selection and AWS credentials, the graph covers first deploy, existing deploy reuse, reset, explicit destroy, and skip-destroy.
Destroy requires TEST_GRAPH_DESTROY_BRANCH_ENVIRONMENT or TESTGRAPH_DESTROY_BRANCH_ENVIRONMENT in addition to AWS selection.

assertions.Local, GitHub Actions, and AWS lifecycle: missing cluster deploy, existing cluster reuse without recreation, reset, explicit teardown, and skip teardown.

evidence: test_graph/support/tg6_lifecycle_support.py centralizes local-github-action/AWS target/backend metadata, AWS opt-in checks, credential checks, and destroy intent checks.
test_graph/sources/Tg6GithubActionLifecycle*.py validates local-github-action missing provision, existing deploy reuse, marker evidence, reset, skip-destroy, guarded destroy, and explicit destroy.
test_graph/sources/Tg6GithubActionLifecycleContextJbang.java validates JBang env:[*] context projection for the GitHub Actions lifecycle provision output.

test_graph/sources/Tg6AwsLifecycle*.py validates default guarded AWS no-op behavior, explicit selected AWS provision/deploy/reset/skip-destroy, and destroy requiring both AWS selection/credentials and destroy intent.
test_graph/sources/Tg6AwsLifecycleContextJbang.java validates JBang context projection for both guarded AWS context and selected AWS environment outputs.
references/environment-repositories.md and references/github-actions.md document the new graph names, AWS opt-in variable, credential guard, and destroy guard.
